assertions.name: consumer_reported_value_is_the_plancherel_weight
assertions.source: alpha_em_b2_scalar_c_probe.py stdout reports w_(4,1)(q0) = 0.12862000417524688333 and its source builds _q_dimension(shape,q)**2/_q_factorial(sum(shape),q). Recomputing d_q^2/[5]_q! independently here confirms the consumer's number IS the Plancherel-family weight -- which is what the corrected audit claims and what its own verdict string denies by calling it Markov.

assertions.name: molien_move_on_this_axis_exceeds_one_percent
assertions.source: |molien/plancherel - 1| = 0.422331436188186430685356308989002433427434880257603283011851 at lambda=[4, 1]. The threshold is a legibility floor, not a physical scale: it asserts only that the qou-oots family choice is not a rounding effect on the alpha_EM axis. The actual move is ~42%.

description: Bean qou-oots. Triages the weight family under the alpha_EM B2 scalar c. alpha_em_b2_scalar_c_probe.py pins on d_q^2/[5]_q! at lambda=(4,1) and its verdict calls that 'the canonical MARKOV normalization' -- but d_q^2/[n]_q! is the PLANCHEREL-family (historical Wedderburn) weight, while the Markov weight is the Ocneanu y_lambda. This probe evaluates all three families at that one partition and reports the ratios, so the size of the qou-oots family choice on this axis is on the record. The consumer uses a SINGLE partition's weight as an absolute normalisation, not a same-n ratio, so the cancellation that makes dim_q^2/[n]_q! -> dim_q^2/D^2 a no-op for the beta_EW consumers is NOT available here. NOT a claim that c is wrong: c = (Markov norm)/(Hodge polarization norm) and the Hodge denominator is openly unsupplied, so c is not a delivered number.

family_change_factors.note: molien/plancherel = f^lam * q^{-kappa} / d_q at this lambda, since both carry the same 1/[n]_q!. The move is NOT small and does NOT cancel: this consumer normalises on ONE partition, so there is no same-n ratio for a lambda-independent factor to drop out of, and Molien's q^{-kappa} is lambda-dependent besides. The Markov row is the family the consumer's verdict NAMES; it is a third, different number, which is the point.
